questions.question: Reading Eq a => [a] -> a -> Bool by the method above, what should you read FIRST?
options: [a], because it's the first thing after the arrow
Eq a =>, in isolation, before applying the ordinary arrow-by-arrow rule to anything after it
Bool, because the result is the most important part
It doesn't matter what order you read the pieces in
questions.explanation: The template states this as a fixed first step: the constraint is read as its own sentence — 'for any type a that supports ClassName's operations' — before the ordinary left-to-right arrow rule is applied to the rest of the signature.
optionFeedback: [a] is the first ordinary argument, but it comes after the constraint has already been read and set aside as a precondition on a, not as an argument itself.
Correct — this is the fixed order: constraint first, in isolation, then the arrows.
The result type matters, but reading it first without first knowing what a is allowed to be skips necessary context.
Order matters precisely because => and -> are different kinds of thing — mixing up which is read as a constraint and which as an argument produces a wrong reading of the whole signature.
